description: THE ALTERNATE-INDEX CASE (gate G45), and the case that proves the cross-reference pad belongs to the harness and not to the fixture (gate G16). app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:34-39 declares ONE file with TWO keys - SELECT XREF-FILE ASSIGN TO XREFFILE, RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-CARD-NUM, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID - and app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:29-32 binds that one cluster twice in one step, XREFFILE on the base KSDS and XREFFIL1 on the alternate-index PATH over the same base. :204 moves TRANCAT-ACCT-ID into FD-XREF-ACCT-ID and 1110-GET-XREF-DATA at :394-395 reads KEY IS FD-XREF-ACCT-ID, so the ACCOUNT ID is the lookup key and the CARD NUMBER is the result. This case therefore seeds XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 from the IDENTICAL fixture reference - cardxref.txt, all fifty rows, in the file's own order - because they are two access paths over one dataset. No second file, no second copy and no re-sorted variant appears anywhere in this case; inventing one would be the 'second table' G45 forbids, and it would also hide the very defect the case is designed to catch. ANTI-POSITIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION. cardxref.txt is ordered by XREF-CARD-NUM, its base KSDS key, and NOT by XREF-ACCT-ID, so an implementation that shortcuts 'account k is row k-1' still passes a carelessly chosen case. The three accounts here are chosen so that it cannot: account 00000000001 is at 0-based cardxref row 48, account 00000000002 at row 2 and account 00000000050 at row 0 - the first near the end of the file and the last at its very front, the exact inverse of positional order. Every card number below was found by matching XREF-ACCT-ID at 1-based bytes 26-36 and reading XREF-CARD-NUM from bytes 1-16 of that same row: 9680294154603697 for account 1, 0923877193247330 for account 2 and 0500024453765740 for account 50. A positional shortcut would instead have produced rows 0, 1 and 49, whose cards are 0500024453765740, 0683586198171516 and 9805583408996588 - all three of them wrong in a field this case pins, so the diff count would be three and not zero. Seeding the WHOLE cross-reference rather than three chosen rows is what makes the search real: the alternate key has fifty candidates to discriminate between. THE 36-TO-50 PAD IS THE HARNESS'S, NOT THE FIXTURE'S. CVACT03Y declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) at 1-16, XREF-CUST-ID PIC 9(09) at 17-25, XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at 26-36 and FILLER PIC X(14) at 37-50 - fifty bytes - while every row of cardxref.txt measures exactly thirty-six, the trailing FILLER span being absent from the data. app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt is NOT edited and is NOT pre-padded: this case seeds it by fixture reference, so it contains no cross-reference seed literal at all, and the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, before anything decodes a row. The XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 images in expectedFinalState are fifty characters because fifty is the width the dataset holds once seeded, and parity.FieldDiffer normalises NOTHING at comparison time - an expectation written at thirty-six would be reported as a width mismatch rather than padded away, which is precisely the property that stops a case from passing with its normalisation forgotten. SEEDS, AND HONEST PROVENANCE FOR THE THREE THAT ARE MODIFIED. ACCTFILE is acctdata.txt in full (50 x 300), XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 are cardxref.txt in full (50 x 36 before the pad), and DISCGRP is discgrp.txt in full (51 x 50) - every one of them byte-for-byte unmodified, and every one seeded whole so that this case's negative assertions are real: forty-eight untouched account rows prove only two were rewritten, and fifty-one disclosure rows prove the DEFAULT retry discriminates rather than finding the only row present. TCATBALF is the one modified input and the modification is disclosed rather than buried: all fifty balances in tcatbal.txt are the zoned positive zero 0000000000{, so the raw fixture cannot produce a non-zero TRAN-AMT at any rate, and the three rows seeded here are the genuine tcatbal.txt rows of accounts 1, 2 and 50 - key 17 bytes, TRANCAT-ACCT-ID + TRANCAT-TYPE-CD '01' + TRANCAT-CD '0001', and the real 22-byte trailing span - with TRAN-CAT-BAL alone overridden to 194.00, 158.00 and 492.00. Those three amounts are not invented either: they are the real ACCT-CURR-BAL values of those same three accounts in acctdata.txt, 00000001940{, 00000001580{ and 00000004920{, re-encoded at CVTRA01Y's S9(09)V99 as 0000001940{, 0000001580{ and 0000004920{. Rows are seeded in ascending account order because :28-32 declares TCATBALF ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL and the account-break logic at :194-206 depends on that order. TRANSACT is output only and is never seeded. THE GROUP KEY IS SPACES - A CORRECTION DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. The folder brief claims acctdata's A000000000 is a group id that steers account rows into the DISCGRP A-block. It is not. Verified across all fifty rows against CVACT01Y, A000000000 sits in ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at 1-based 103-112 and ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 is TEN SPACES on 50/50 rows. So :210 moves spaces into FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID, the READ at :416 is keyed '          ' + '01' + '0001' and misses with FILE STATUS '23', :418-419 display both disclosure-group lines, :422 tolerates '00' OR '23' so nothing abends, and :437 moves 'DEFAULT' into an X(10) receiver so the retry key is 'DEFAULT   ' and hits discgrp.txt row 17. DIS-INT-RATE is therefore 15.00, read from bytes 17-22 as '00150{': DIS-GROUP-KEY is SIXTEEN bytes per CVTRA02Y, not seventeen, and a seventeen-byte assumption would shift the rate by one byte and corrupt it. The DEFAULT fallback is this program's fixture-faithful happy path, which is why all three records take it. ARITHMETIC, RE-DERIVED (gates G24, G25, G28). COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = (TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 at :464-465 carries no ROUNDED - the keyword appears zero times in all 28 programs - so the receiver PIC S9(09)V99 truncates, which is BigDecimal at scale 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN and never HALF_UP or HALF_EVEN. Account 1: 194.00 x 15.00 / 1200 = 2.4250 exactly, stored 2.42, zoned 0000000024B - HALF_UP would store 2.43. Account 2: 158.00 x 15.00 / 1200 = 1.9750 exactly, stored 1.97, zoned 0000000019G - HALF_UP and HALF_EVEN BOTH store 1.98, so this record alone rules out both half modes. Account 50: 492.00 x 15.00 / 1200 = 6.1500 exactly, stored 6.15, zoned 0000000061E - a terminating quotient, present as the control that shows the truncation is not itself an error. Each product was recomputed from the fixture bytes rather than copied. THE THREE GENERATED RECORDS. All fourteen CVTRA05Y spans are pinned BY NAME in copybook order and the whole 350-byte image is pinned as well, so a failure localises to one field while the total width still proves the trailing FILLER X(20) was emitted as spaces (gates G19, G20, G21; INTCALC.jcl:39 is RECFM=F,LRECL=350). TRAN-ID runs 2022071800000001, ...000002, ...000003 - contiguous from one and never from 000000, because ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX at :474 precedes the STRING at :476-480 and WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is PIC 9(06) VALUE 0; PARM-DATE is the ten characters of INTCALC.jcl:22 PARM='2022071800' concatenated verbatim and never parsed as a date, giving an exact 10+6=16 byte fit into TRAN-ID PIC X(16). TRAN-CAT-CD is '0005' and not '05  ', because :483 moves the alphanumeric literal '05' into a PIC 9(04) numeric-display receiver. TRAN-SOURCE is 'System' plus four spaces in a PIC X(10) span. TRAN-DESC is the 24-byte STRING prefix - 'Int. for a/c ' is thirteen characters including its trailing space, plus the eleven-digit ACCT-ID - followed by exactly 76 spaces, because STRING at :485-489 writes only the composed bytes and leaves the receiver tail untouched while common.FixedWidthCodec builds the record with every PIC X span space-initialised; the composed prefix is invariably 24 bytes, so the tail is invariant rather than incidental. TRAN-MERCHANT-ID is '000000000' from MOVE 0 into a PIC 9(09), and the three merchant spans are 50, 50 and 10 spaces from MOVE SPACES. EXACTLY TWO REWRITES, AND THE THIRD IS ABSENT BY DESIGN (gate G27, practice B5). 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT is reached from :196 only on an account break with WS-FIRST-TIME NOT = 'Y'. Record 1 is the first break, so :198 merely flips the flag and nothing is rewritten. Record 2 breaks with the flag now 'N', and the rewrite fires at :196 BEFORE :202 repoints FD-ACCT-ID, so it rewrites ACCOUNT 1 with account 1's accumulated total. Record 3 breaks and rewrites ACCOUNT 2. Then end of file: the ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT at :219-220 is UNREACHABLE dead code, because the enclosing PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :188 makes the IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' at :189 always true, so ACCOUNT 50's accumulated interest is never flushed. That defect is preserved verbatim, not fixed, and it is asserted positively: acctdata row 49 is pinned BYTE-IDENTICAL to its seed, ACCT-CURR-BAL still 00000004920{, which no absent expectation could state. The two rows that do change are pinned twice over - all thirteen CVACT01Y fields by name AND the complete 300-byte image - in the order :352-356 performs them: ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL, MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT, MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT, then REWRITE. Account 1 goes 194.00 + 2.42 = 196.42, zoned S9(10)V99 as 00000001964B; account 2 goes 158.00 + 1.97 = 159.97, zoned as 00000001599G; each account has exactly one TCATBALF row, so WS-TOTAL-INT is that account's single monthly interest. Both cycle amounts land on 00000000000{, which in unmodified acctdata they already were - so what this case proves is the REWRITE COUNT and the balance addition, while the ORDER of the three statements is proved observably by case13, which seeds non-zero cycle amounts. (The folder brief points at case11 for that; case11 is the second-'23' abend and writes nothing, so the pointer is corrected here rather than repeated.) ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE is spelt exactly as app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy misspells it, and repairing that spelling here would leave the diff looking for a field the decoder never produces - a silent parity break rather than a loud one, which is why the misspelling is the contract. 1400-COMPUTE-FEES, performed at :216 inside the same IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 guard, is the '* To be implemented' stub at :518-520 and contributes no record, no field and no message. DETERMINISM AND CHANNELS. The eleven expected messages are 1 + 3 x 3 + 1: the run banner at :181, then per record the raw 50-byte TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD image displayed at :193 followed by the two :418-419 fallback lines, then the closing banner at :230. No error line appears, because every open, read, write, rewrite and close succeeds and the return code is 0. TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are the program's only wall-clock values, both taking the same DB2-FORMAT-TS from Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP at :613-626 through :496-498; no 'now' is ever captured. A BATCH_JOB case pins no clock of its own - pinnedClock is a screenRequest member and screenRequest is refused for a batch unit - so ParityHarness.DEFAULT_PINNED_CLOCK applies, fixed at 2022-07-19T23:12:34 after the repository-wide source footer 'Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19' and rendering as the 26-byte 2022-07-19-23.12.34.000000. The folder brief's literal 2022-07-18-00.00.00.000000 is not what the harness produces and is corrected here rather than copied. Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching the app/data/ASCII fixtures, never a platform default. Datasets are addressed only by their carddemo.datasets binding key and never by a fully-qualified, dotted mainframe dataset name - which parity.ParityCase's binding-key pattern could not accept in any case, so gate G46 is enforced by the model and not merely observed here - and the unit is reached as account.AccountInterestCalcJob.calculateInterest(String, SysoutSink) with no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP layer in the path (gate G51). SHAPE AND PROVENANCE. The members are those of parity.ParityCase, which deserialises strictly: the write-order channel is expectedWrites and the post-run dataset contents are expectedFinalState - there is no expectedRecords member, and the folder brief's name for it is corrected here so the file binds. Every observed row is addressed, because parity.FieldDiffer reports an unaddressed row as EXTRA_RECORD wherever it sits: 3 TCATBALF, 50 ACCTFILE, 50 XREFFILE, 50 XREFFIL1 and 51 DISCGRP rows on the final-state channel, read back in ascending record-image order, which for these five key-at-offset-zero datasets is key order. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the COBOL paragraphs cross-checked against the CVTRA01Y, CVTRA02Y, CVTRA05Y, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts, the INTCALC.jcl DD, PARM and RECFM contracts, and the real ASCII fixtures. It was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment. review_rules returns the single line 'No user rules provided.', which is the whole document, so no project rule governs this file and none has been invented; the migration plan's best-practice substitutes bind instead - B1 no placeholders, B3 reference inputs immutable, B4 corrections documented, B5 dead code preserved, B7 determinism, B8 explicit over implicit, B11 offsets read mechanically and B12 honest provenance.
